answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable stake before trading, linked to a persistent history of honest work. Trust grows like a pulse that must keep beating: an identity earns standing only through repeated successful transactions over time, not by registering many new names. If it cheats, the stake is slashed and its reputation falls. Creating a raven flock of fake identities is therefore expensive, since every copy must pay, wait, and build history separately. An attacker cannot simply give the same actor a fresh umber coat, because cost and delay multiply with each duplicate.
